title: Take one bottle from a row of five without knocking any over
instruction: Put the red bottle in the tray without knocking over any of the other bottles.
context: Taking one item from a tightly packed shelf (pharmacy, lab reagents, retail) without disturbing the rest, where one bump can topple several.
setup: A wooden shelf board (12 x 30 x 2 cm) is fixed with its centre 31 cm in front of the arm bases, spanning 5 cm right to 25 cm left of their midline. Five glass bottles (4 cm wide, 12 cm tall, 0.15 kg) stand on it in a left-right row 30 cm in front of the bases, 1.2 cm apart: the middle one is red and 10 cm left of the midline, the others amber. A blue tray (10 x 10 cm inside, 2 cm walls) is taped 15 cm in front of the bases, 25 cm left of the midline.
scoring: 0 if any bottle ever tilts more than 45 degrees during the trial, even if it is stood back up. Red bottle upright (within 15 degrees) in the tray: 1.0, or 0.5 if an amber bottle ever tilts more than 10 degrees or ends more than 1 cm from its start. Red bottle upright and 5 cm or more from its start but not in the tray: 0.25. Otherwise 0. In the tray: centre inside the walls, resting on the floor.
reset_notes: Stand the bottles back on their marks, 1.2 cm apart; a 1.2 cm spacer makes this quick.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the bottles are solid cylinders. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2), so a pushed bottle tips rather than slides. Glass breakage is not simulated: a tilt past 45 degrees counts as a fall.
